title: Microsoft Teams: Meeting Shared Files for meeting participants and Facilitator
summary: Hold: the briefing assigns file selection exclusively to meeting organisers without evidence; the roadmap says users, not which meeting role can add files. It also calls Facilitator availability the only documented lever, although the cited page documents a separate Loop prerequisite and control. The roadmap details and the feature-specific documentation gaps otherwise check out.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: It is the meeting organiser, not an administrator, who chooses the files.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Meeting Shared Files" "organizer" Facilitator' and '"Meeting Shared Files" Teams Facilitator files links default sharing external participants organizer admin policy'; opened facilitator-teams. The roadmap says users; no role restriction was found.
claims.fix: Replace 'It is the organiser, not an administrator, who chooses the files, so oversharing becomes a meeting-by-meeting decision that a service owner cannot see in advance.' with 'The roadmap says users add the content; it does not identify which meeting roles can do so.' Use 'users' instead of 'organisers' for factual statements about who selects or adds files in the summary, Why it matters and impact rationale. Keep organiser-focused advice as advice.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block reaches the Facilitator availability control.
claims.quote: In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. ... In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked $true is a MicrosoftTeams command for changing app state in the tenant.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app ... -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant. ... Type: Boolean
claims.fix: Use 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked <Boolean>' and add to the row note: 'The reference describes IsBlocked as the tenant app state, but Example 3 describes $true as unblocking; confirm the intended state before using automation.' The command and parameter exist, but the reference does not consistently explain the printed value.

claims.claim: Facilitator availability controls govern access to Facilitator, rather than documenting a switch for adding Meeting Shared Files.
claims.quote: As an admin, you control whether Facilitator is available to your entire organization or to a certain group of users.

claims.claim: Groups can be allowed Facilitator using an app permission policy and app-centric management.
claims.quote: To allow Facilitator for users, a new app policy needs to be created and then assigned to users. ... You can then assign the policy to your entire tenant or to a select group of users.
claims.fix: Replace the policy wording in the row note and Governance controls with 'Facilitator access for groups can be managed with app-centric management. In tenants migrated to app-centric management, app permission policies are no longer available.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management, which states: 'After you switch to this feature, you can't access, edit, or use permission policies.' The Facilitator page supports the original wording but the management page qualifies it.

claims.claim: Facilitator's allow or block control is the only documented lever.
claims.quote: Loop experiences in Teams need to be turned on in order for Facilitator to be used in meetings. ... You can manage this control using the IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled setting in PowerShell.
claims.fix: Replace 'Facilitator's allow or block control is the only documented lever' in changes with 'Facilitator availability is a documented alternative lever'. Replace 'The one documented control is Facilitator's availability' in Governance controls with 'The table documents Facilitator's availability as an alternative lever'. Do not claim that this is the only documented Facilitator control.
